justification: One of the most directly relevant datasets for studying Croatian parliamentary debates across the 2000s, 2010s, and beginning of the 2020s. Created by Michal Mochtak, Josip Glaurdić, and Christophe Lesschaeve (2022), it contains more than 500,000 speeches from five complete parliamentary terms (2003–2020). It provides cleaned and preprocessed speech transcripts, dates, parliamentary sessions, agenda items, speaker identities, political party affiliations, and policy classifications. Particularly suitable for longitudinal analysis of political discourse, party competition, legislative agendas, and parliamentary polarization.

returned_title: ParlaMint 5.0: Multilingual Comparable Corpora of Parliamentary Debates
justification: A major multilingual parliamentary debate dataset distributed through the CLARIN.SI research infrastructure. Includes Croatian parliamentary proceedings alongside those of other European legislatures. The Croatian component provides historical coverage beginning in 2003 and extending into the 2020s. It includes structured speech transcripts and extensive parliamentary metadata, making it particularly valuable for studying Croatian political discourse over time and comparing Croatian parliamentary debates with those in other European countries.

returned_title: ParlaMint 4.1: Multilingual Comparable Corpora of Parliamentary Debates
justification: A multilingual collection of parliamentary debate transcripts covering 29 European countries and autonomous regions, including Croatia. The collection generally extends through mid-2022, although individual country coverage varies. It provides parliamentary speech texts with metadata on speakers, political parties, gender, parliamentary roles, and government or opposition status. Useful for analyzing Croatian debates during the 2010s and early 2020s, particularly in comparative European research.

returned_title: ParlaMint 2.1: Multilingual Comparable Corpora of Parliamentary Debates
justification: An earlier release of the CLARIN ParlaMint parliamentary corpus collection, including Croatian parliamentary proceedings. The Croatian component covers debates from November 2016 to May 2020. It provides structured parliamentary transcripts with speaker and party metadata. Particularly useful for investigating Croatian parliamentary politics during the late 2010s, including government-opposition interactions and political discourse before and during the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic.

returned_title: ParlaSpeech-HR 2.0: Parliamentary Spoken Corpus of Croatian
justification: A Croatian parliamentary speech dataset combining transcripts from the ParlaMint corpus with recordings of Croatian parliamentary proceedings. Developed by Nikola Ljubešić, Peter Rupnik, and Danijel Koržinek, it provides approximately 3,000 hours of parliamentary speech recordings. Especially valuable for research requiring both spoken audio and text, including political communication, speech recognition, prosody, rhetorical delivery, and computational analysis of Croatian parliamentary debates.

returned_title: ParlaSpeech 3.0: Richly Annotated Spoken Parliamentary Corpora of Croatian, Czech, Polish, and Serbian
justification: A collection of spoken parliamentary corpora released in 2025, covering Croatian alongside Czech, Polish, and Serbian. It combines parliamentary recordings with transcripts and metadata derived from ParlaMint and adds automatic annotation layers. Relevant for studying Croatian parliamentary speech during the periods represented by its source recordings. Particularly suitable for speech technology, political rhetoric, linguistic analysis, and comparisons between parliamentary speech and written transcripts. The linked page describes the dataset and its release.

returned_title: ParlaSent-BCS: Sentiment-Annotated Parliamentary Debates from Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, and Serbia
justification: A specialized dataset containing sentiment-annotated sentences extracted from parliamentary debates in Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Serbia. The Croatian material originates from parliamentary proceedings covering 2003–2020. Sentences are annotated using a six-level sentiment classification scheme and can be connected to their original parliamentary speeches through identifiers. Particularly useful for analyzing political negativity, emotional polarization, partisan conflict, and sentiment in Croatian parliamentary language.

returned_title: ParlaCAP: Dataset for Tracking Political Agenda-Setting Across European Parliaments
justification: A comparative parliamentary dataset extending ParlaMint 5.0 with automatically assigned policy topics and sentiment information. It includes Croatian-language parliamentary material and transforms parliamentary speeches into a tabular format suitable for quantitative analysis. Particularly valuable for examining how the Croatian Parliament's policy priorities, political agendas, and rhetorical negativity changed across the 2000s, 2010s, and early 2020s, subject to the Croatian component's available coverage.

returned_title: CROCorp: Corpus of Parliamentary Debates in Croatia, GESIS Edition (2003–2020)
justification: The GESIS research data repository edition of CROCorp, published by Mochtak, Glaurdić, and Lesschaeve in 2022. It contains cleaned and preprocessed Croatian parliamentary debate transcripts from 2003–2020, covering five parliamentary terms and more than 500,000 speeches. Includes metadata about elected representatives and their political parties. This is an alternative repository and an earlier version of the CROCorp dataset, rather than an independent collection. Useful for researchers who prefer obtaining data through an established social science data archive.

returned_title: CROCorp: Corpus of Parliamentary Debates in Croatia, University of Luxembourg Repository
justification: Institutional repository record maintained by the University of Luxembourg for CROCorp version 1.1.1. Documents the Croatian parliamentary debate corpus spanning 2003–2020 and provides access to its accompanying documentation and codebook. The codebook explains variables relating to speeches, parliamentary terms, dates, agenda topics, speakers, and political affiliations. This is a documentation and discovery resource for the same CROCorp dataset, rather than a separate corpus.

returned_title: ParlaMint.ana 2.1: Linguistically Annotated Multilingual Parliamentary Debates
justification: A linguistically annotated version of the ParlaMint parliamentary proceedings collection that includes Croatian parliamentary debates. It enriches transcripts with linguistic information such as tokenization, sentence segmentation, grammatical categories, morphological features, and syntactic analysis. The Croatian component of this release focuses on parliamentary debates from November 2016 to May 2020. Particularly useful for computational linguistics, political language analysis, and research into grammatical and rhetorical patterns in Croatian parliamentary discourse.

returned_title: Croatian Bureau of Statistics – PC-Axis Statistical Databases
justification: Official statistical database maintained by the Croatian Bureau of Statistics. Contains datasets covering Croatia during the 2000s, 2010s, and 2020s. Topics include population, employment, wages, GDP, tourism, agriculture, industry, environmental statistics, and foreign trade. Particularly useful for analyzing long-term economic, demographic, and social changes within Croatia.

returned_title: Croatian Bureau of Statistics – Historical Statistical Databases
justification: Provides access to historical statistical datasets for Croatia, including the 2003 Agricultural Census, 2011 Population Census, and 2020 Agricultural Census. Also includes statistics on employment, household consumption, poverty, transportation, and regional development. Useful for comparing Croatia across the three decades.

returned_title: World Bank – World Development Indicators: Croatia
justification: Comprehensive collection of annual socioeconomic indicators for Croatia covering 2000–2020 and beyond. Includes GDP, inflation, unemployment, population, education, healthcare, poverty, energy consumption, and environmental indicators. Suitable for longitudinal research and comparisons with other European countries.

returned_title: World Bank DataBank – Croatia Development Indicators
justification: Interactive database allowing researchers to select Croatian economic, demographic, and development indicators for specific years. Supports comparisons between the 2000s, 2010s, and 2020s, with downloadable data and customizable time-series analysis.

returned_title: Croatian Bureau of Statistics – Agricultural Census 2003
justification: Official agricultural census dataset documenting Croatia's agricultural sector in 2003. Provides information on agricultural holdings, land use, livestock, and farming activities. Useful as a baseline for examining changes in Croatian agriculture during the following decades.

returned_title: Croatian Bureau of Statistics – Agricultural Census 2020
justification: Official dataset covering Croatian agriculture in 2020, including agricultural land, livestock, irrigation, farm labor, machinery, and agricultural production. Particularly valuable for comparing agricultural conditions in the 2020s with the 2003 Agricultural Census.

returned_title: Croatian Bureau of Statistics – Population Census 2011
justification: Official demographic census providing detailed information about Croatia's population in 2011. Includes demographic characteristics and population distributions. Useful for studying demographic changes between the 2000s and 2010s and establishing a reference point for comparisons with the 2020s.

returned_title: Eurostat – Population and Employment in National Accounts
justification: Official European statistical dataset covering Croatian population and employment within the national accounts framework. Supports research into labor-market developments, employment patterns, productivity, and demographic changes during the 2010s and 2020s. Historical observations may also support comparisons with the 2000s.

returned_title: Eurostat – Industrial Production Statistics for Croatia
justification: Official European statistical metadata and associated datasets concerning Croatian industrial production. Includes industrial activity indicators useful for examining manufacturing performance, industrial growth, and economic fluctuations across the 2000s, 2010s, and 2020s, subject to the availability of individual series.

returned_title: Croatian Open Data Portal – Datasets Available Through the European Data Portal
justification: Collection of thousands of Croatian public-sector datasets covering government administration, public finances, transportation, municipal budgets, and other areas. Includes records from the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly useful for researching local governance, public expenditure, and regional developments within Croatia.

returned_title: Federal Reserve Economic Data – Croatia Population
justification: Annual population time series for Croatia, sourced from the World Bank. Includes observations from the 2000s onward, supporting analysis of population decline, demographic trends, and long-term changes across the 2000s, 2010s, and 2020s.

returned_title: World Bank – Croatia GDP per Capita
justification: Annual GDP per capita data for Croatia, including observations from 2000 onward. Useful for studying changes in economic prosperity during the 2000s, the effects of the global financial crisis, economic developments during the 2010s, and recovery and growth during the 2020s. The database also supports international comparisons.

returned_title: Croatian Bureau of Statistics – Subnational Statistics
justification: Official regional statistical datasets covering Croatian counties and other geographical divisions. Useful for investigating regional disparities, population changes, economic development, and social conditions. Particularly relevant for research comparing different areas of Croatia across the 2000s, 2010s, and 2020s, depending on individual table coverage.

returned_title: Croatian Bureau of Statistics – Tourism Statistics
justification: Official tourism statistics covering visitor arrivals, overnight stays, and related tourism indicators in Croatia. Suitable for analyzing the development of Croatian tourism during the 2000s and 2010s, the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, and subsequent changes in tourism activity.

returned_title: Croatian Bureau of Statistics – Employment and Wages
justification: Official Croatian labor-market statistics covering employment and wage indicators. Useful for investigating labor-market changes during the 2000s, economic restructuring in the 2010s, and employment and wage developments in the 2020s. Available historical coverage varies by statistical table.

returned_title: Croatian Bureau of Statistics – GDP and National Accounts
justification: Official national accounts database covering Croatia's economic performance. Includes GDP and related macroeconomic indicators. Particularly useful for studying economic growth, recession periods, structural economic changes, and recovery across the 2000s, 2010s, and 2020s.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – 2021 and 2025 Federal Elections
justification: One of the most relevant sources for studying political ideology in Germany during the 2020s. GLES provides representative surveys covering political self-identification, left-right ideological positioning, party preferences, voting behavior, political polarization, and attitudes toward democracy. Its 2021 and 2025 federal election datasets allow researchers to examine ideological differences among German voters and changes between elections.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – 2023
justification: A nationally representative German social survey covering political attitudes, ideological orientations, social values, and demographic characteristics. The 2023 edition is particularly useful for investigating relationships between political ideology and factors such as education, age, socioeconomic status, and regional identity. It supports research into left-right political identification and broader ideological divisions within German society.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Data and Documentation
justification: Provides access to multiple ALLBUS survey waves, including those conducted in the 2020s. The surveys contain measures of political attitudes, ideological self-placement, democratic values, political participation, and attitudes toward immigration. Particularly valuable for studying ideological change in Germany and comparing political orientations across population groups and survey years.

returned_title: Politbarometer 2025 – Cumulated Dataset
justification: A comprehensive dataset of German political opinion surveys conducted throughout 2025 by Forschungsgruppe Wahlen. It includes respondents' political preferences, assessments of political parties, left-right ideological placement of parties, voting intentions, and attitudes toward major political issues. Particularly useful for studying ideological polarization, the Alternative for Germany (AfD), party competition, and public opinion surrounding the 2025 federal election.

returned_title: Politbarometer – German Political Opinion Surveys
justification: A major source of recurring political opinion surveys in Germany. Provides annual cumulative datasets covering the 2020s, including political attitudes, party preferences, voting intentions, and evaluations of political leaders. Its repeated measurements are especially useful for tracking shifts in ideological preferences and political polarization over time.

returned_title: Politbarometer 1977–2024 – Cumulative Political Opinion Dataset
justification: A longitudinal dataset combining selected political opinion measures from German Politbarometer surveys through 2024. Includes party preferences, political participation, satisfaction with democracy, and attitudes toward major political issues. Particularly valuable for comparing ideological developments during 2020–2024 with historical patterns and examining longer-term changes in German political preferences.

returned_title: European Social Survey (ESS) – Round 10 (2020–2022)
justification: A high-quality comparative European survey containing observations from Germany. Includes an explicit left-right ideological self-placement scale, political trust, party preferences, attitudes toward immigration, social values, and democratic participation. Researchers can filter observations to Germany to study ideological differences across demographic groups and compare German political ideology with that of other European countries.

returned_title: European Social Survey (ESS) – Round 11 (2023–2024)
justification: Provides survey data on political and social attitudes across European countries during 2023–2024, including Germany. Relevant variables include left-right ideological identification, political trust, democratic attitudes, electoral participation, and preferences regarding social issues. Useful for examining contemporary ideological polarization in Germany and comparing findings with earlier ESS rounds.

returned_title: Chapel Hill Expert Survey (CHES) – 2024 European Political Party Positions
justification: An expert-coded dataset measuring the ideological positions of European political parties, including major German parties. The 2024 survey includes general left-right ideology, economic left-right positioning, and the Green/Alternative/Libertarian versus Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist (GAL-TAN) dimension. It also covers positions on immigration, redistribution, environmental policy, populism, and European integration. Especially useful for comparing the ideological profiles of CDU/CSU, SPD, Greens, FDP, AfD, and other German parties.

returned_title: Chapel Hill Expert Survey – European Party Position Trend Dataset (1999–2024)
justification: A longitudinal dataset measuring European political parties' ideological positions across multiple survey waves, including 2024. It enables researchers to track ideological movement among German political parties, including changes in economic ideology, cultural conservatism, nationalism, and European integration preferences. Particularly valuable for studying the evolution of Germany's party system and the ideological positioning of established and emerging political movements.

returned_title: Manifesto Project Dataset – Political Party Ideology and Election Manifestos
justification: A major comparative dataset analyzing the policy positions expressed in political party election manifestos. It includes German political parties and elections during the 2020s. Researchers can examine ideological positioning, economic policy preferences, immigration, nationalism, social welfare, environmental policy, and democratic values. Particularly useful for measuring ideological shifts in German parties using their official political programs rather than voter surveys.

returned_title: Manifesto Project Dataset – Version 2025a
justification: A documented release of the Manifesto Project's comparative party-policy dataset. It includes coded election manifestos from German political parties, with coverage extending into the 2020s. Researchers can construct ideological measures, compare left-right party positions, examine changes in issue emphasis, and investigate ideological competition between mainstream parties and the AfD. Particularly useful for quantitative analysis of party ideology during recent German federal elections.

returned_title: Chapel Hill Expert Survey – SPEED-CHES 2020 and 2023
justification: A collection of specialized expert surveys examining European political party positions during major political developments in the 2020s. Includes surveys concerning responses to the COVID-19 pandemic and the war in Ukraine. German political parties are included in the broader European coverage. Useful for examining how ideological orientations relate to party positions on specific political crises and for analyzing differences between authoritarian, nationalist, conservative, liberal, and progressive political orientations.

returned_title: GESIS German Election Research Data Collection
justification: A centralized research data portal providing access to German federal and state election surveys, including GLES and Politbarometer datasets from the 2020s. Relevant measures include political attitudes, ideological orientations, voting behavior, party identification, and perceptions of political institutions. Especially useful for locating additional election-specific datasets and investigating geographic and demographic differences in German political ideology.

returned_title: Universities in the Federal Republic of Germany, 1949–2001 (GESIS)
justification: A historical dataset documenting higher education in West Germany from 1949 to 2001, including the entire 1960s. It contains longitudinal statistics on universities, student enrollment, first-year students, and institutional developments. Based on official German statistics, it is particularly valuable for investigating the expansion of higher education during the 1960s.

returned_title: Development of Higher Education in East and West Germany, 1960–1990
justification: A historical statistical dataset comparing higher education in East Germany (GDR) and West Germany (FRG). Includes observations for 1960, 1965, and 1970, covering numbers of universities, enrolled students, first-year students, graduates, doctoral examinations, and academic personnel. Particularly useful for comparing the development of higher education under the two German political systems.

returned_title: Historical Statistics: Higher Education, Vocational Schools and Educational Institutions in Germany, 1960–2000
justification: A collection of historical educational statistics containing time series on German universities, university teachers, student enrollment, and first-year students beginning in 1960. It also includes vocational school classes and different types of educational institutions. Particularly relevant for examining both higher education and further or vocational education during the 1960s.

returned_title: Historical Statistics: Relative School and University Attendance in West Germany, 1952–1975
justification: A historical statistical study of school and university attendance in the Federal Republic of Germany between 1952 and 1975. It includes the 1960s and provides information on educational participation and changes in student populations. Useful for studying the expansion of access to secondary and higher education and changes in educational participation rates.

returned_title: Historical Statistics: Education and Training in the German Democratic Republic, 1960–1975
justification: A historical statistical collection covering education and training in East Germany, including tables organized by training group and gender for 1960–1975. Relevant for analyzing vocational training, educational participation, and gender differences during the 1960s. Particularly useful for research on the structure and development of education in the GDR.

returned_title: Total Number of Students by Type of Higher Education Institution and Nationality (German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space)
justification: An official German government statistical table containing historical student enrollment figures, with records for former West Germany beginning in 1947/1948. It provides information on student numbers by higher education institution type and nationality. Suitable for examining changes in university participation and the expansion of German higher education during the 1960s.

returned_title: Bildung im Zahlenspiegel 1985: Historical Education Statistics in West Germany
justification: An official historical statistical publication from the German Federal Statistical Office. Its higher education tables include student enrollment by institution type for the winter semesters 1960/61 and 1965/66 through 1969/70. The publication provides historical education statistics useful for analyzing university enrollment, institutional differentiation, and educational expansion during the 1960s. The URL leads to the statistical library rather than directly to the publication.

returned_title: Statistical Yearbook of the German Democratic Republic, 1972: Universities, Admissions and Graduates
justification: A historical statistical table from the GDR's 1972 Statistical Yearbook containing annual university admissions and graduate numbers for 1960–1970. It distinguishes between full-time, distance, and evening study programs, making it particularly valuable for research on higher education and continuing education in East Germany throughout the 1960s. The table also includes gender-specific figures for selected years.

returned_title: Historical Higher Education Statistics: University Enrollment and Examinations, 1953–1967
justification: A digitized collection of historical statistical materials containing information on German universities, student enrollment, higher education examinations, and educational developments during the 1950s and 1960s. Includes historical tables covering university examinations from 1953 to 1967 and international comparisons of student populations. Useful for investigating academic participation and qualifications during the early and middle 1960s.

returned_title: Preconditions of the Formation of Public Opinion in the Federal Republic of Germany, 1964
justification: Highly relevant dataset consisting of four national cross-sectional surveys of the West German electorate conducted between May and July 1964. Covers attitudes toward the federal government, political parties, domestic and foreign policy, evaluations of politicians, and political knowledge. Particularly useful for studying political attitudes, public opinion formation, and political preferences in 1960s West Germany.

returned_title: German Pre- and Post-Election Study, 1969
justification: A major electoral survey examining political behaviour and attitudes surrounding the 1969 West German federal election. Includes voting behaviour in the 1965 election, intended voting in 1969, expectations about election outcomes, political participation, party preferences, and attitudes toward political issues. Particularly valuable for investigating electoral change and political alignments during the late 1960s.

returned_title: Issue Dimensions and Voting Decision (April 1969)
justification: GESIS dataset collected between April and May 1969 investigating political controversies, voting intentions, and party preferences. Includes evaluations of CDU/CSU, SPD, FDP, and NPD, attitudes toward recognition of East Germany, foreign policy, radicalism, and economic issues. Also contains retrospective voting behaviour from the 1965 federal election. Especially useful for analysing ideological divisions, issue-based voting, and attitudes toward German division.

returned_title: Public Opinion Surveys: West Germany, November 1968
justification: Historical public opinion survey collection conducted in West Germany in November 1968 and archived by ICPSR. Relevant for examining political attitudes and public opinion during a period of political and social change. Can be used alongside the December 1968 surveys and the 1964 public opinion surveys to investigate changes in attitudes during the decade.

returned_title: Public Opinion Surveys: West Germany, December 1968
justification: Public opinion surveys of the adult West German population conducted in December 1968. Includes opinions about the federal chancellor, president, political parties, economic conditions, inflation, community problems, and government responses. Particularly useful for studying political leadership evaluations, economic perceptions, and public satisfaction with government during the late 1960s.

returned_title: Cologne Election Study (Dortmund, Arnsberg-Soest, Heilbronn, Munich; November 1961)
justification: GESIS electoral survey conducted in November and December 1961, containing 1,501 respondents. Examines political interest, party identification, evaluations of politicians, election campaign perceptions, coalition preferences, voting history, and changes in party sympathy. Particularly valuable for investigating political behaviour and partisan identification in early 1960s West Germany. Forms part of a three-wave panel study.

returned_title: Cologne Election Study (Federal Republic, November 1961)
justification: West German electoral study conducted following the 1961 federal election. Investigates public attitudes toward political parties, politicians, the party system, governing coalitions, elections, and broader social developments. Useful for examining voter preferences and evaluations of the political system during the Adenauer era. Provides a nationally oriented counterpart to regional Cologne election studies.

returned_title: Political and Economic Attitudes of the Population of Berlin (May–December 1965)
justification: GESIS dataset investigating political and economic attitudes among residents of West Berlin during 1965. Includes assessments of Berlin's political development, economic conditions, and public policy. Particularly relevant for examining political attitudes in a city directly affected by Cold War tensions and German division.

returned_title: Political and Economic Attitudes of the Population of Berlin (February–March 1967)
justification: Survey of West Berlin residents conducted in February and March 1967. Covers political knowledge, political participation, party preferences, voting intentions, satisfaction with the mayor and federal chancellor, and perceptions of Western powers' interest in Berlin. Also includes economic expectations, organizational membership, and media consumption. Particularly useful for studying the relationship between political attitudes, economic concerns, and Cold War geopolitics.

returned_title: Resonance of the Population to the Election Campaign and the Result of the Federal Parliament Election 1969
justification: GESIS dataset examining public reactions to the 1969 West German federal election campaign and election results. Includes political interest, attendance at campaign meetings, satisfaction with election outcomes, evaluations of parties and politicians, coalition preferences, and attitudes toward a possible SPD–FDP government. Particularly valuable for analysing electoral engagement, political communication, and reactions to changes in government.

returned_title: German Post-War Election Database (GPWED), 1949–1969
justification: Highly relevant historical dataset containing municipality-level results for West German federal parliamentary elections between 1949 and 1969, including the elections of 1961, 1965, and 1969. Enables detailed analysis of voting patterns, political party support, electoral geography, and the development of West Germany's democratic political system during the 1960s. Particularly useful for examining regional political differences and electoral changes.

returned_title: ParlGov – Parliaments and Governments Database
justification: Comparative political dataset documenting political parties, parliamentary elections, government cabinets, and coalition formation in established democracies, including West Germany during the 1960s. Provides structured information on government composition, party representation, election results, and cabinet changes. Particularly valuable for studying the transition from Christian Democratic governments to the first Social Democratic-led federal government in 1969.

returned_title: Comparative Political Data Set (CPDS), 1960–2023
justification: Longitudinal dataset containing political and institutional indicators for democratic countries, including West Germany throughout the 1960s. Includes variables related to government composition, parliamentary representation, political parties, electoral systems, and political institutions. Suitable for examining West Germany's government structure and comparing its political system with other European democracies during the Cold War.

returned_title: Comparative Political Data Set – Historical Data Archive
justification: Provides downloadable historical versions of the Comparative Political Data Set, including datasets beginning in 1960. Contains country-year observations concerning political institutions, governing parties, electoral outcomes, and government composition. Particularly useful for quantitative research on changes in West German government and political organizations throughout the 1960s.

returned_title: Manifesto Project Database – Political Party Election Programs
justification: Extensive dataset of political party election manifestos and their coded policy positions across democratic countries since 1945. Includes German political parties participating in the federal elections of 1961, 1965, and 1969. Enables systematic investigation of ideological differences, policy priorities, and political competition between organizations such as the CDU/CSU, SPD, and FDP during the 1960s.

returned_title: German Bundestag Open Data – Parliamentary Records and Members Since 1949
justification: Official German parliamentary open-data collection providing machine-readable parliamentary documents, plenary proceedings, and biographical information about Bundestag members since 1949. Covers the parliamentary terms of the 1960s and supports research into legislative activity, political representatives, parliamentary institutions, and government-opposition relationships in West Germany.

returned_title: German Federal Election Results, 1949–2013 – Wahlen in Deutschland
justification: Historical election database offering downloadable results of German federal elections at constituency, state, and national levels. Includes the 1961, 1965, and 1969 Bundestag elections, with data available in statistical formats including Stata and Excel. Useful for analyzing party competition, parliamentary seat distribution, electoral geography, and changes in political representation during the 1960s.

returned_title: German Bundestag – Historical Parliamentary Data Handbook
justification: Official historical statistical collection documenting the organization, membership, and activities of the German Bundestag since 1949. Includes parliamentary statistics and chronological information covering the 1960s. Particularly relevant for studying parliamentary structures, government formation, legislative activity, political representation, and institutional development in West Germany.

returned_title: Fraktionen im Deutschen Bundestag, 1949–2005 – Parliamentary Party Group Records
justification: Research dataset containing edited meeting records of parliamentary party groups in the German Bundestag. Includes CDU/CSU records from 1949 to 1976, SPD records from 1949 to 1980, and FDP records from 1949 to 1983, providing coverage of the entire 1960s. Particularly valuable for studying political party organizations, internal parliamentary decision-making, coalition negotiations, party leadership, and government-opposition relationships.

returned_title: Members of the German Bundestag Since 1949 – btmembers Dataset
justification: Structured parliamentary membership dataset derived from official Bundestag records. Provides information on representatives serving in the German federal parliament since 1949, including all parliamentary terms during the 1960s. Offers downloadable data in CSV and Excel formats, making it useful for examining political careers, party affiliations, parliamentary membership, and changes in political representation.

returned_title: REPDEM – Representative Democracy Data Archive
justification: Comparative historical dataset documenting governments, parliaments, political parties, and political institutions in parliamentary democracies from 1945 onward. Includes West Germany during the 1960s. Contains information about cabinet formation, government duration, party representation, parliamentary institutions, and election results. Particularly useful for studying coalition governments, parliamentary democracy, and political stability.

returned_title: Political Parties, Presidents, Elections, and Governments (PPEG)
justification: Comparative political dataset combining information on political parties, election results, government cabinets, and political executives across democracies. Its historical coverage begins in 1942 and includes postwar West Germany. Suitable for analyzing political organizations, electoral competition, governing coalitions, cabinet composition, and changes in executive power during the 1960s.

returned_title: German Federal Election 1961 – Official Electoral Statistics
justification: Official historical electoral statistics published by Germany's Federal Returning Officer for the 1961 Bundestag election. Provides party vote totals, vote shares, parliamentary seat allocations, and constituency-level election results. Particularly useful for examining the political system at the beginning of the 1960s, including the electoral performance of the CDU/CSU, SPD, and FDP.

returned_title: German Democratic Republic – Volkskammer Elections, 1950–1989
justification: Official German Federal Archives collection documenting elections to the East German Volkskammer between 1950 and 1989. Includes archival materials concerning the electoral system and political institutions of the German Democratic Republic during the 1960s. Particularly valuable for investigating the Socialist Unity Party's political dominance, the National Front electoral system, and the institutional differences between East and West Germany. Primarily an archival source collection rather than a ready-made statistical dataset.

returned_title: Members of the German Bundestag, 1946–1972 – Historical Biographical Documentation
justification: Historical research collection documenting members of Germany's political and parliamentary elite between 1946 and 1972. Covers political representatives active throughout the 1960s and provides biographical information relevant to the study of political leadership, parliamentary organizations, and elite recruitment. Useful for reconstructing political networks and examining continuity and change in West German political institutions. It is primarily a biographical research resource rather than a standardized quantitative dataset.

returned_title: German Bundestag – Parliamentary Documentation and Historical Proceedings
justification: Official collection of German parliamentary documentation, including plenary proceedings and legislative documents dating back to the first Bundestag electoral term in 1949. Contains primary-source material from the 1960s concerning government policy, legislative debates, parliamentary parties, and political institutions. Useful for analyzing the functioning of parliamentary democracy and the activities of political organizations during the period.

returned_title: Reproductive Behavior of Women and Couples: Socioeconomic and Psychosocial Determinants, 1990 Population Survey
justification: Highly relevant GESIS dataset examining reproductive behavior among women aged 15–45 residing in East Berlin. Data were collected between September 1990 and October 1991, covering the transition from the German Democratic Republic (GDR) to reunified Germany. The survey investigates socioeconomic and psychosocial determinants of reproductive decisions. Particularly valuable for studying reproductive health and family planning during the final months of the GDR and the immediate post-reunification period.

returned_title: German Fertility and Family Survey 1992
justification: Nationally representative fertility and family survey conducted between May and September 1992, involving 10,012 respondents aged 20–39. Approximately half of the interviews were conducted in the former GDR. The dataset contains 846 variables covering fertility intentions, family formation, reproductive behavior, partnership histories, and socioeconomic circumstances. Particularly useful for comparing reproductive patterns in former East and West Germany following reunification.

returned_title: Reproductive Behavior of Women and Couples: Supplementary Survey of Women Undergoing Abortion in East Berlin, 1990–1991
justification: The GESIS documentation for the 1990–1991 reproductive behavior survey identifies a related supplementary study archived under ZA6386. This supplementary survey focuses specifically on women undergoing abortions at an East Berlin clinic during the study period. It is particularly relevant for investigating abortion decisions and reproductive healthcare during German reunification. The URL points to the verified parent-study metadata, which references ZA6386, rather than a separately verified supplementary-study landing page.

returned_title: Historical Abortion Statistics: East Germany, 1945–1990
justification: Historical statistical compilation covering induced abortions, live births, abortion ratios, and reproductive indicators in East Germany through 1990. Particularly useful for examining long-term changes in abortion prevalence under the GDR's reproductive health policies. Provides historical context for interpreting reproductive behavior observed in surveys conducted during the 1990s. Some figures are estimates, so researchers should examine the accompanying methodological notes.

returned_title: East Germany: Abortions, Live Births, and Abortion Percentages by Region, 1972–1990
justification: Regional historical dataset containing abortion statistics, live births, and abortion percentages across East Germany from 1972 through 1990. Enables geographical comparisons of reproductive outcomes across regions including East Berlin, Brandenburg, and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. Particularly relevant for studying regional differences in reproductive health during the final decades of the GDR and establishing a baseline for post-reunification research.

returned_title: Life in the GDR 1990 (Leben in der DDR 1990)
justification: GESIS survey conducted in January 1990 within the German Democratic Republic, including the districts of Potsdam, Leipzig, and Schwerin. Examines health, partnerships, social security, living conditions, and social transformation. Although not exclusively focused on reproductive health, it provides valuable contextual information about healthcare and family circumstances during the GDR's final year. Useful for studying how broader social conditions influenced reproductive decisions.

returned_title: Life in Eastern Germany 1992 (Leben Ostdeutschland 1992)
justification: GESIS survey of 1,516 adults living in former East Germany, conducted between April and May 1992. Contains 309 variables examining social conditions and adaptation to political and economic transformation. Although reproductive health is not its primary focus, the dataset provides contextual information for investigating family well-being and the social consequences of reunification. It belongs to a longitudinally comparable series of surveys covering the early and mid-1990s.

returned_title: World Population Monitoring 1996: Selected Aspects of Reproductive Rights and Reproductive Health
justification: United Nations statistical publication containing international reproductive health indicators, including reported legal abortions around 1990 and reproductive rights statistics. Includes German abortion statistics for 1992 and provides a framework for comparing reproductive health trends across countries. Useful as a supplementary source for examining Germany's reproductive health situation immediately after reunification. The figures are primarily national rather than specific to the former GDR.

returned_title: Politbarometer East 1991: Cumulated Dataset
justification: GESIS survey dataset examining public opinion in eastern Germany during 1991. Includes questions about abortion legislation and political representation of respondents' preferences concerning abortion regulation. Particularly relevant for understanding public attitudes toward reproductive rights in the former GDR following reunification. This dataset measures political attitudes rather than clinical reproductive health outcomes.

returned_title: Politbarometer East 1993: Cumulated Dataset
justification: Public opinion dataset covering eastern Germany in 1993, including questions about abortion regulation and political preferences. Useful for studying changing attitudes toward reproductive rights during the early post-reunification period. Can complement historical abortion statistics and fertility surveys by providing information about the political and social context surrounding reproductive healthcare.

returned_title: Health 1990 (Gesundheit 1990)
justification: Highly relevant dataset collected in June 1990 in the German Democratic Republic (GDR). Covers health-related information from individuals aged 14 and older. Provides a historical source for examining population health around German reunification. Archived by GESIS Data Archive.

returned_title: Partners III – Employed Persons 1990 (Partner III – Berufstätige 1990)
justification: Survey conducted in the GDR during the first half of 1990. Classified by GESIS under specific diseases, disorders and medical conditions, particularly concerning HIV/AIDS, sexual behavior, reproductive health and disease-related awareness. Useful for researching public health attitudes and HIV/AIDS prevention in the final year of the GDR.

returned_title: Partners III – Apprentices 1990 (Partner III – Lehrlinge 1990)
justification: Survey conducted in the GDR in 1990 examining relationships, sexuality and sexual behavior among young people during the AIDS epidemic. Classified under specific diseases, disorders and medical conditions. Relevant for investigating HIV/AIDS awareness and sexual health risks among young East Germans.

returned_title: Nuclear Energy and Environmental Consciousness 1990 (Kernenergie und Umweltbewusstsein 1990)
justification: Dataset based on a 1990 survey of 704 respondents across the five eastern German states. Classified by GESIS under specific diseases, disorders and medical conditions. Includes perceptions of health risks, environmental hazards and nuclear energy. Particularly useful for studying perceived environmental health threats in the former GDR, although it does not primarily measure diagnosed diseases.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2014
justification: Longitudinal collection of German population surveys, including eastern Germany beginning in 1991. Contains information about chronic illnesses, physical and psychological health, disabilities, healthcare utilization and HIV/AIDS awareness. The 1991–1998 survey waves are relevant for investigating disease-related conditions in the former GDR during the 1990s. Geographic identifiers enable East–West comparisons.

returned_title: System of Social Indicators for the Federal Republic of Germany: Health
justification: Historical health-indicator dataset covering Germany from 1950 to 2013, including the 1990s. Includes causes of death, ongoing illnesses, disabilities, sickness absence, medical treatment and medication use. Useful for examining historical changes in health conditions around reunification, subject to the availability of separate eastern German observations.

returned_title: Life in Eastern Germany 1992 (Leben Ostdeutschland 1992)
justification: Population survey conducted in eastern Germany in 1992, shortly after the dissolution of the GDR. Includes questions concerning health, health-related lifestyles, social security and living conditions. Useful for contextualizing health and disease-related experiences during the transition from the GDR, although it is not primarily a clinical disease dataset.

returned_title: German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Adults (DEGS) and Historical German Health Surveys
justification: Official Robert Koch Institute study landing page providing information about German population health surveys and their historical comparisons. Particularly relevant because the earlier Health Survey East was conducted in 1991–1992 among residents of the former GDR, while the nationwide 1998 survey included eastern German participants. The surveys cover cardiovascular conditions, chronic diseases, health risk factors and healthcare utilization. Historical microdata access may require contacting the Robert Koch Institute.

returned_title: German Cancer Registry Data – Epidemiological Cancer Statistics
justification: Dataset resource describing cancer incidence, mortality, prevalence and survival statistics from the German Centre for Cancer Registry Data. Its geographic and disease-specific indicators are relevant for investigating cancer patterns in eastern Germany following reunification. The listed resource begins in 1999, so its direct coverage of the earlier 1990s and historical GDR territory is limited.

returned_title: GESIS Microcensus Trendfile
justification: Harmonized German microcensus data covering multiple decades, including 1991, 1993 and 1995–1999. Contains health-related variables and demographic information, potentially allowing analysis of residents of the former GDR after reunification. Useful for population-level studies of health inequalities and associated risk factors, although detailed disease-specific information may be limited.

returned_title: German Fertility and Family Survey 1992 (Deutscher Fertility and Family Survey 1992)
justification: Highly relevant dataset collected in 1992 examining family formation, fertility intentions, marriage, household composition, partnership histories, and attitudes toward children in reunified Germany. It provides an opportunity to investigate family life among people from the former German Democratic Republic (GDR) during the early post-reunification period. Particularly useful for studying changes in marriage, childbearing, and family structures following German reunification.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Family and Changing Gender Roles II – ISSP 1994
justification: A 1994 international survey explicitly including separate samples from eastern Germany (1,097 respondents) and western Germany (2,324 respondents). It examines attitudes toward marriage, family responsibilities, gender roles, women's employment, childcare, and household arrangements. Particularly valuable for comparing family values inherited from the GDR with those prevalent in western Germany four years after reunification.

returned_title: Life in the GDR 1990 (Leben in der DDR 1990)
justification: Directly relevant historical survey conducted in January 1990, during the final year of the German Democratic Republic. It investigates social conditions, personal relationships, partnerships, living arrangements, and life satisfaction among GDR residents. The geographical coverage includes the Potsdam, Leipzig, and Schwerin districts. This dataset provides a particularly useful baseline for understanding family and partnership experiences immediately before reunification.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core): Longitudinal Household Data, 1984–2021
justification: A major longitudinal household survey that expanded to East Germany in 1990, allowing researchers to follow individuals and households from the former GDR throughout the 1990s. It contains information on marital status, household composition, partnerships, children, employment, income, and living conditions. Especially useful for investigating how reunification influenced family formation, marital stability, household economics, and gender roles over time.

returned_title: Population, Population Movement, Households and Families in the Federal Republic of Germany, 1947–1999
justification: Historical statistical dataset covering population development, demographic changes, private households, families, marital status, and numbers of children. Its geographical coverage includes the new eastern German federal states and East Berlin following reunification. The dataset is useful for examining demographic trends during the 1990s and comparing family structures in eastern and western Germany. It provides aggregate statistical evidence rather than individual-level interviews.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Family and Changing Gender Roles I–V Cumulation
justification: Harmonized dataset combining international surveys conducted in 1988, 1994, 2002, 2012, and 2022. The 1994 component includes respondents from former East Germany and examines marriage, cohabitation, divorce, household responsibilities, gender roles, and attitudes toward children. Useful for analyzing whether attitudes toward marriage and family associated with the GDR persisted or changed after reunification. Researchers can isolate the 1994 eastern German observations for analysis.

returned_title: Statistical Overviews of Social Policy in Germany Since 1945: Soviet Occupation Zone / GDR
justification: Historical statistical compilation focusing specifically on the Soviet occupation zone and the German Democratic Republic between 1945 and 1989. It provides contextual evidence on the development of social policies under the GDR, which is useful for investigating the institutional environment surrounding family life, childcare, and social protection. Although published after the 1990s, its historical coverage makes it relevant for understanding the family-policy structures inherited by eastern Germany at reunification.

returned_title: Bamberg Panel on Nonmarital Cohabitation (Bamberger NEL-Panel)
justification: Longitudinal study examining nonmarital partnerships, marriage, and changing attitudes toward family formation. Its survey waves include observations around 1990, making it potentially useful for understanding broader German changes in cohabitation and marriage during the reunification period. However, its geographical coverage and suitability for specifically studying former GDR residents require verification before use.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS)
justification: Major German social survey program that expanded its coverage to the former East Germany in 1991. Surveys conducted throughout the 1990s provide information on family-related attitudes, social values, household characteristics, and demographic circumstances. The program is particularly useful for comparing eastern and western German attitudes toward marriage, family responsibilities, and social change after reunification. The URL leads to the official GESIS survey data portal, where individual ALLBUS waves can be located.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2019
justification: One of the most comprehensive longitudinal datasets for studying social stratification in Germany during the 2010s. Contains annual individual- and household-level information on income, wealth-related indicators, education, employment, occupational status, migration background, household composition, and social mobility. Particularly suitable for examining economic inequality, class differences, intergenerational mobility, and changes in socioeconomic status between 2010 and 2019.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 2018
justification: A nationally representative survey of Germany's adult population covering social structure, socioeconomic characteristics, attitudes, and social group differences. Includes information relevant to education, occupational position, income, social class, religion, and demographic characteristics. Useful for investigating social stratification and relationships between socioeconomic position and social attitudes in Germany in 2018.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 2016
justification: Provides representative survey data on German society in 2016, including occupational categories, educational attainment, socioeconomic characteristics, political attitudes, and perceptions of different social groups. Relevant for investigating class structures, social divisions, educational inequalities, and differences between demographic groups.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 2014
justification: Provides cross-sectional information on social structure and attitudes in Germany during 2014. Supports research on socioeconomic groupings, occupational stratification, education, social background, and demographic differences. Can be combined analytically with other ALLBUS survey waves to investigate changes in social stratification throughout the 2010s.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 2012
justification: Contains representative survey data on German social structure and attitudes in 2012. Relevant variables include education, employment, occupational classifications, demographic characteristics, and indicators of social position. Particularly useful for studying socioeconomic differentiation and social group membership during the early 2010s.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2023
justification: A harmonized cumulative dataset combining multiple ALLBUS survey waves, including those conducted during the 2010s. Enables longitudinal comparisons of repeated cross-sectional measures of occupational status, education, socioeconomic position, demographic characteristics, and social attitudes. Particularly valuable for identifying changes in class composition, social inequalities, and group differences across Germany between 2010 and 2019.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Social Inequality V, 2019
justification: A survey specifically designed to investigate social inequality and stratification. Includes Germany alongside other participating countries. Covers perceived social class, socioeconomic inequalities, occupational status, social mobility, distributive justice, and attitudes toward income differences. Particularly relevant for examining subjective and objective dimensions of social stratification. Note that the German component of this ISSP 2019 module was collected in 2020, making it useful primarily as a measure of conditions and perceptions around the end of the 2010s.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Social Inequality I–V Cumulation, 1987–2019
justification: A harmonized international dataset combining five waves of the ISSP Social Inequality module. Includes observations for Germany and supports historical comparisons of perceived social class, occupational hierarchies, income inequality, social mobility, and attitudes toward redistribution. Particularly valuable for examining how German social stratification changed between earlier decades and the late 2010s.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS) – Starting Cohort 4: Grade 9, 2010
justification: A German longitudinal educational dataset following students who were in ninth grade in 2010. Includes information on parental socioeconomic background, educational pathways, school characteristics, migration background, and transitions into vocational training or higher education. Highly relevant for investigating educational stratification, intergenerational inequality, and the reproduction of social class during the 2010s.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS) – Starting Cohort 5: First-Year Students, 2010
justification: Tracks individuals entering German higher education in 2010. Contains information relevant to parental education, socioeconomic origins, educational trajectories, academic experiences, and transitions into employment. Useful for analyzing social inequalities in access to higher education, differences between socioeconomic groups, and educational mobility during the 2010s.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS) – Starting Cohort 6: Adults
justification: A longitudinal survey of adults in Germany with observations throughout the 2010s. Covers educational histories, employment trajectories, occupational mobility, lifelong learning, and socioeconomic background. Particularly valuable for understanding how education and labor-market experiences contribute to social stratification and mobility across different adult population groups.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS) – Starting Cohort 2: Kindergarten, 2011
justification: A longitudinal study of children entering kindergarten in Germany in 2011. Includes information on family socioeconomic status, parental education, migration background, learning environments, and educational development. Suitable for examining how social inequalities emerge during childhood and how differences between socioeconomic and demographic groups influence educational opportunities.

returned_title: German Family Panel (pairfam), 2008–2021
justification: A longitudinal German dataset covering family relationships, partnerships, household structures, and intergenerational relationships, with extensive observations during the 2010s. Includes demographic and socioeconomic characteristics that support analyses of social groupings by family status, generation, education, and social background. Particularly useful for studying relationships between family structures, socioeconomic inequality, and social mobility.

returned_title: German Family Panel (pairfam) – Scientific Use Files, Waves 1–13
justification: Provides longitudinal information on partnership formation, family dynamics, fertility, intergenerational relationships, and socioeconomic characteristics in Germany. The waves covering 2010–2019 are useful for investigating demographic stratification, social differences in family formation, and relationships between educational attainment, employment, and household composition.

returned_title: German Student Social Survey – Pooled Data Set, 1982–2016
justification: A harmonized dataset covering the economic and social circumstances of students in German higher education, including survey waves from the 2010s. Contains information on parental socioeconomic background, educational origins, income, employment, housing, migration-related characteristics, and living conditions. Particularly relevant for analyzing educational stratification, social inequalities among university students, and differences in higher education participation across social groups.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Social Inequality Module Series
justification: Provides access to the ISSP surveys devoted specifically to social inequality, including the 2019 module and earlier comparative waves. Relevant for examining Germans' perceptions of class divisions, occupational prestige, income inequality, social mobility, and distributive justice. Particularly useful for researchers interested in subjective social stratification and comparative perspectives on Germany.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2020, EU Edition
justification: A longitudinal household panel covering the entire 2010–2019 period, with an additional observation year in 2020. Includes income, education, employment histories, household characteristics, health, and socioeconomic indicators. Well suited to studying poverty, income inequality, social class, migration-related inequalities, household stratification, and changes in socioeconomic status over the decade.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS) – Combined Data Portfolio
justification: An official collection of German longitudinal educational datasets covering multiple age groups and educational stages during the 2010s. Enables comparisons of educational attainment, family background, migration background, employment transitions, and socioeconomic opportunities. Particularly useful for investigating educational inequality and intergenerational social stratification across different population cohorts. Scientific Use Files are available to researchers under data-use agreements.

returned_title: Second European Union Minorities and Discrimination Survey (EU-MIDIS II), 2016
justification: Conducted by the European Union Agency for Fundamental Rights (FRA), this survey collected data in 2015–2016 on ethnic minorities and people with immigrant backgrounds across Europe, including Germany. The German sample included 1,419 respondents of Turkish and Sub-Saharan African backgrounds. Topics include ethnic discrimination, employment, housing, education, harassment, hate crimes, police interactions, and social integration. Particularly relevant for studying minority experiences in Germany during the mid-2010s.

returned_title: EU-MIDIS II: Minorities and Discrimination Survey Data Explorer (2016)
justification: An interactive dataset provided by the EU Agency for Fundamental Rights. It allows researchers to examine survey findings on ethnic minorities and immigrants in Germany and compare them with other European countries. Data can be filtered by country, age, gender, and immigrant generation. Particularly useful for investigating discrimination, social inclusion, and differences between first- and second-generation immigrants in 2016.

returned_title: German Microcensus (Mikrozensus), 2010–2019
justification: Germany's official annual household survey provides extensive demographic and socioeconomic information. Data from 2010–2019 can be used to study populations with a migration background, including ethnic and national-origin minority groups. Variables cover citizenship, migration background, education, employment, household composition, and living conditions. Its large sample size makes it particularly valuable for analyzing relatively small minority populations and demographic changes throughout the 2010s. Access to detailed microdata is restricted.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2020
justification: A longitudinal household panel dataset administered by the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin). It includes observations throughout the 2010s and contains information on migrants, refugees, and people with immigrant backgrounds. Relevant variables include employment, income, educational attainment, family structure, social participation, and subjective well-being. Specialized migration and refugee samples make it particularly useful for investigating socioeconomic inequalities and integration trajectories among minority populations.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 2018
justification: A nationally representative social survey administered through GESIS. The 2018 edition provides information on social attitudes, demographic characteristics, national identity, and aspects of immigration and social inequality. ALLBUS includes measures relevant to ethnocentrism, attitudes toward immigrants, and relationships between majority and minority populations. Useful for examining public perceptions of ethnic and religious minorities in Germany during the late 2010s.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), Historical and Cumulative Datasets
justification: GESIS provides access to repeated cross-sectional surveys covering Germany, including survey waves conducted during the 2010s. Topics include immigration, ethnocentrism, religious identity, attitudes toward foreigners, social distance, and minority integration. The cumulative datasets support comparisons across multiple years, making them especially useful for analyzing changes in German attitudes toward ethnic, national-origin, and religious minorities between 2010 and 2018.

returned_title: ALLBUS: Ethnocentrism, Minorities, and Migration Variables
justification: The ALLBUS thematic documentation identifies variables specifically addressing ethnocentrism, minorities, and migration. Measures include attitudes toward foreigners, perceptions of immigration, social distance from ethnic minorities, attitudes toward Islam, support for mosque construction, and perceptions of refugees. These variables can be located in relevant 2010s ALLBUS survey waves and used to investigate prejudice, religious tolerance, and minority acceptance in Germany.

returned_title: Second European Union Minorities and Discrimination Survey (EU-MIDIS II) – Survey Registry
justification: A research registry entry documenting the EU-MIDIS II survey conducted in 2016. It provides information about the survey's coverage, methodology, target populations, and data provider. The survey includes Germany and focuses on ethnic minorities and immigrants, particularly experiences of discrimination and social exclusion. Useful for identifying survey documentation and investigating access to research data suitable for secondary analysis.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP): Migration and Refugee Samples
justification: The SOEP includes specialized migration and refugee samples introduced and expanded during the 2010s. These samples provide detailed information about immigrant populations, including individuals arriving from European countries and refugees who entered Germany during the decade. Researchers can examine labor-market integration, educational attainment, economic inequality, household conditions, and social integration. Particularly useful for studying changes associated with Germany's 2015–2016 refugee arrivals.

returned_title: Eating Habits and Nutritional Status in Quedlinburg, 1985–1989: Part 3 – Dietary Habits of Pregnant Women
justification: Highly relevant primary dataset from the German Democratic Republic (GDR). Contains dietary information collected from pregnant women attending Quedlinburg District Hospital during the late 1980s. Records summarize individual meals and food consumption over a one-week period. Part of a ten-study research project examining nutrition among pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers, and infants. Archived by GESIS and available for academic research.

returned_title: Eating Habits and Nutritional Status in Quedlinburg, 1985–1989: Part 2 – Sociological Survey of Non-Pregnant Women
justification: Primary research dataset examining nutritional status and eating habits among women aged 18–35 in the GDR. Data were collected during 1987–1988 from patients attending gynecological consultations in Quedlinburg. Particularly useful for studying dietary behavior, nutrition-related social factors, and differences between pregnant and non-pregnant women in East Germany.

returned_title: GDR Household Budget Statistics, 1988–1989 (Statistik des Haushaltsbudgets)
justification: One of the most directly relevant datasets for investigating food consumption in East Germany immediately before reunification. Contains household-level information on food expenditure, beverages, household income, and consumption of self-produced goods. Covers November 1988 through October 1989, with 40,594 household observations. Includes workers, agricultural cooperative members, and pensioners. Particularly valuable for analyzing food expenditure patterns, socioeconomic differences, and household consumption. Access to microdata is managed by GESIS.

returned_title: GDR Income Survey of Workers' and Employees' Households, 1988 (Einkommensstichprobe)
justification: Representative household survey conducted in the GDR in 1988, covering approximately 30,000 households and 80,000 individuals. Includes household income, demographic characteristics, and socioeconomic conditions. Although not a direct dietary intake survey, it provides valuable contextual data for investigating economic determinants of food consumption and nutritional inequalities in the GDR during the late 1980s.

returned_title: GDR Statistical Yearbook 1986 – Per Capita Consumption of Selected Foods and Beverages
justification: Historical statistical tables published by the GDR's official statistical administration. Includes annual per capita consumption figures for major food categories, including meat, fish, eggs, milk, cheese, butter, margarine, vegetables, potatoes, flour, and other products. Provides observations for 1980 and several subsequent years through 1985. Especially useful for reconstructing national dietary patterns and examining changes in food availability and consumption during the 1980s. Data are presented as historical tables rather than downloadable microdata.

returned_title: GDR Statistical Yearbook 1984 – Historical Food Consumption Statistics
justification: Official GDR statistical series containing per capita food consumption figures for 1980–1983 alongside earlier historical observations. Covers meat, dairy products, fats, cereals, vegetables, fruit, and other food categories. Useful for establishing baseline food consumption patterns in the early 1980s and comparing nutritional trends with later GDR statistical publications.

returned_title: Statistical Overview of Per Capita Consumption of Selected Food and Luxury Products in the GDR
justification: Historical statistical compilation presenting per capita consumption figures for selected foods and beverages in East Germany. Includes observations from the 1980s and facilitates comparisons across years. Relevant for reconstructing long-term patterns of food consumption, particularly meat, dairy products, and other staple foods. This is a secondary statistical compilation rather than an original survey dataset.

returned_title: Life in the GDR, 1990 (Leben in der DDR 1990)
justification: GESIS survey dataset collected in January 1990, during the final year of the German Democratic Republic. Covers living conditions, health, healthy lifestyles, consumer goods availability, economic conditions, and satisfaction with everyday life. Includes respondents from the Potsdam, Leipzig, and Schwerin districts. Although dietary intake is not its primary focus, the survey provides important contextual information for examining nutrition-related living conditions during the transition from socialism to reunification.

returned_title: Statistical Overviews of Social Policy in Germany Since 1945: Soviet Occupation Zone and GDR
justification: Historical dataset compiled by André Steiner and archived by GESIS. Contains statistical time series describing socioeconomic conditions and social policy in East Germany, covering the GDR period and extending into the 1990s. Relevant for investigating the social and economic context of nutrition, including household living standards and welfare conditions. This is a supplementary source rather than a direct dietary consumption dataset.

returned_title: HISTAT: Basic Data on the Development of Health Conditions in Germany, 1816–2010
justification: Historical statistical dataset archived by GESIS, containing health indicators for Germany, including the former GDR. Its long chronological coverage allows comparisons between East Germany during the 1980s and unified Germany during the 1990s. Useful for studying population health outcomes potentially associated with nutritional conditions, although it does not directly measure individual food consumption.

returned_title: Nutrition Situation of the Population in the Former East Germany: Results of Household Budget Surveys in 1989
justification: Research publication reporting results from representative nutritional household surveys conducted in the GDR in 1989. Contains findings on energy intake, dietary fats, carbohydrates, proteins, and eating habits. Particularly relevant because it analyzes nutritional conditions immediately before reunification. Published in 1992, it provides a direct source of quantitative findings from historical nutrition surveys. The link leads to a research article presenting survey results, not a standalone downloadable dataset.

returned_title: Health 1990 (Gesundheit 1990) – German Democratic Republic
justification: A highly relevant dataset specifically focused on health in the German Democratic Republic in 1990. Conducted by the Department of Medical Sociology at the Institute for Social Hygiene and Health Care Organization in Berlin, the survey covers individuals aged 14 and older. It provides valuable evidence about health and well-being during the GDR's final year. Available through the GESIS Data Archive.

returned_title: Life in the GDR 1990 (Leben in der DDR 1990)
justification: A January 1990 survey examining living conditions, social security, health, healthy lifestyles, housing, and general life satisfaction in the GDR. Covers the districts of Potsdam, Leipzig, and Schwerin. Particularly useful for investigating subjective well-being, perceived quality of life, and social conditions immediately before German reunification.

returned_title: HISTAT: Basic Data on the Development of Health Conditions in Germany, 1816–2010
justification: A historical statistical dataset containing official health indicators for Germany, including the German Democratic Republic. Covers mortality rates, age-specific mortality, life expectancy, and other indicators of population health. Its extensive historical coverage makes it particularly suitable for examining health developments throughout the 1980s and comparing the GDR with reunified Germany during the 1990s.

returned_title: Welfare Survey 1990 – East Germany (Wohlfahrtssurvey 1990 – Ost)
justification: A survey conducted between October and December 1990 examining objective living conditions and subjective quality of life among East Germans. Includes assessments of personal health, financial circumstances, employment, housing satisfaction, and general well-being. Contains 735 observations and 227 variables. Particularly relevant for studying health satisfaction and quality of life during the transition from socialism to reunification.

returned_title: Statistical Overview of Social Policy in Germany Since 1945: Soviet Occupation Zone / GDR
justification: A historical statistical compilation covering social policy in the Soviet occupation zone and the GDR, with observations extending from 1939 to 1996. Draws on official GDR health statistics, including annual publications from 1965 to 1988. Useful for researching health care provision, social protection, and the institutional conditions influencing population health during the 1980s.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core): Data 1984–2016
justification: A major longitudinal household survey covering health, employment, income, living conditions, and subjective well-being. Although the study began in West Germany in 1984, it expanded to the GDR in June 1990, before reunification. Particularly valuable for tracing changes in health satisfaction, economic security, and general well-being among former GDR residents throughout the 1990s.

returned_title: Life in East Germany 1993 (Leben Ostdeutschland 1993)
justification: A survey investigating social conditions and subjective well-being in eastern Germany three years after reunification. Includes questions about the importance of health, social security, employment, housing, healthy lifestyles, and overall life satisfaction. Particularly useful for comparing post-reunification experiences with the 1990 GDR survey and examining how political and economic transformation affected well-being.

returned_title: System of Social Indicators for Germany: Health, 1950–2013
justification: A comprehensive collection of health-related social indicators compiled by GESIS.
